scope: SDK008 source and retained Python lifecycle smoke acceptance only; no native qualification or resource admission.

resolvedFinding.resolution: The launcher requires fresh runtime and owner roots before forking. The real qualifier requires a fresh runtime while permitting the just-created owner root, then verifies the current PID/birth owner and exact source seal/runtime description before mkdir. Pure tests follow the actual detached main/body/qualify.main path and separately reject direct unowned entry and reused roots.

lifecycleReview: The one-shot double fork creates an independent session, closes inherited descriptors and publishes an OS birth identity acknowledgement. Initial fork reap and owner acknowledgement are bounded to the launch deadline; uncertain state refuses a relaunch.

Command ownership begins with verified direct parentage, then retains macOS PID/birth identities for observed descendants across distinct groups/reparenting. Each signal revalidates that identity. Path-only matches only create ambiguity and can never authorize signals.

Source cleanup targets known PIDs individually, escalates TERM/KILL under existing deadlines, and refuses success without original-group absence, leader reaping, observed-identity absence and no ambiguous candidates/errors/signals. No process-name or path-wide kill was introduced.

Command-start evidence is fsynced and bounded and records only own argv/cwd/timeout/identity. OWNER records executable/argv. TERMINAL binds the saved RESULT bytes. Environment reads are not introduced.

The original overall clock starts before detachment; owner output/evidence count toward existing packet/log caps. STOP validates nonce and identity. Exceptions preserve the first failure without automatic retry.
limitations: Discovery is sampled: closure proves absence of observed owned birth identities and no ambiguous exact-runtime-path candidates, not discovery of every possible pathless orphan between snapshots.

The saved smoke exercises Python descendants and POSIX launcher termination. It does not establish native Swift/compiler lifecycle behavior or survival of host-wide force termination, SIGKILL, machine loss or disk failure.
Native SDK 26+9 execution, source-to-binary proof and full result/owner terminal acceptance remain unqualified. Earlier SDK006 failure and held SDK007 source remain preserved.
No physical asynchronous CxxBackend, native FRT0, iOS, public activation, release or performance credit is granted.
